_doc: PUBLICATION-1 (owner, 2026-11-15): every repository of the org is public under USL-1.0 (free for non-commercial use, commercial licence for commercial use, share-alike, no patents asserted, defensive disclosure), and publishing is a procedure the code runs, not a decision anyone re-makes. Read by foundation/publication.py: `python3 -m foundation publication --check|--audit|--plan|--flip`. `--check` is part of the doctrine step. A flip is refused until the audit is clean over full history; a history that cannot be read in full (shallow clone) is `unmeasured`, never clean. The procedure and lessons below are data the check enforces; changed only by a reviewed PR.

procedure.does: scan every commit on every branch for secret patterns; shallow history is unmeasured
list tripwire paths; each must be in ops/publication/reviewed.json with a disposition (publish, move, remove)
required files present, SPDX id present, licence text identical across repos (license/scripts/check-copies.mjs)
gh repo edit <org>/<repo> --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences, in flip_order, then verify unauthenticated
procedure.gate: IC-GATE-001 residue: needs an org-admin token; default in effect is stay private until the audit is clean

routes: tick Worker with the GitHub App consent screen (POINT-AND-CLICK-1)
credential.default_in_effect: repositories stay as they are; no step fails open

lessons.lesson: A cloud code session's GitHub tools cannot change repository visibility and gh is barred there; the flip is owned by a server-side route holding ORG_ADMIN_TOKEN, never by a session.
Session clones are shallow; a secret scan of them proves nothing about history. Shallow means unmeasured.
Publishing exposes full history and forks and caches cannot be undone; the flip refuses until the audit is clean.
The licence text is immutable and a protected path; publication never edits it, and the copies must stay identical.
A refused action is recorded and the next route taken; it is never re-worded past the same check.
